case_summary.summary: Reviewer accepted removal of the purely descriptive Non-toxic condition and its incident edge, but rejected deletion of Vapor and High confinement because cross-type semantic overlap was not accepted as redundancy and High confinement was treated as causally contributory. The updated graph confirms C2 and En1->C2 were removed, while C1 and C4 were kept, with C4 additionally linked downstream to nitrogen accumulation.

planning_patterns.matched_rule: Do not remove a node for redundancy based only on semantic overlap across different node types; remove only truly descriptive-only nodes with no needed causal role.
planning_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Reject node deletions when the redundancy claim depends mainly on cross-type similarity rather than clear structural nonuse.

planning_patterns.matched_rule: Remove descriptive-only condition nodes that add no necessary local causal role and have no downstream mechanism links.
planning_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Accept deletion of isolated descriptive conditions when they do not contribute to the supported causal pathway.

planning_patterns.reviewer_reason: This condition contributed to the accumulation of nitrogen
planning_patterns.matched_rule: Keep a condition when it has a supported downstream causal function; the descriptive-only deletion rule applies only when no mechanism role exists.
planning_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Reject deletion of a condition if it helps explain release, dispersion, or accumulation in the local mechanism.

planning_patterns.proposed_change: Delete edge En1 -> C1 (Nitrogen has Vapor).
planning_patterns.matched_rule: Do not remove an edge when the underlying redundancy claim for the connected node is unsupported, especially if based only on cross-type overlap.
planning_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Keep attachment edges when the associated node remains valid and the redundancy rationale is not structurally supported.

planning_patterns.proposed_change: Delete edge En1 -> C2 (Nitrogen has Non-toxic).
planning_patterns.matched_rule: Delete incident edges when their target descriptive-only node is removed.
planning_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Accept edge deletion as a direct follow-on when the connected node is correctly deleted.

planning_patterns.proposed_change: Delete edge En2 -> C4 (Reactor has High confinement).
planning_patterns.matched_rule: Do not delete an attachment edge when the connected condition node is retained as causally relevant.
planning_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: If a node remains in scope, keep its grounding edge unless there is a separate reason to remove it.

diagnosis_patterns.observed_pattern: A condition appears semantically similar to content already represented by another node type.
diagnosis_patterns.diagnosis_interpretation: Reviewer treated cross-type similarity as insufficient for a redundancy diagnosis. Redundancy should be framed structurally, not just semantically.
diagnosis_patterns.supporting_rule: Diagnose redundancy only for nodes that are descriptive-only and lack a necessary causal role.
diagnosis_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Do not diagnose a node as redundant solely because an event, entity, and condition express related ideas.

diagnosis_patterns.observed_pattern: A condition is purely descriptive and structurally isolated from the mechanism.
diagnosis_patterns.diagnosis_interpretation: This was treated as background characterization rather than causal mechanism, so it was appropriately diagnosed as removable redundancy.
diagnosis_patterns.supporting_rule: Descriptive-only condition nodes with no necessary downstream mechanism links should be removed.
diagnosis_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Diagnose isolated descriptive attributes as low-value graph detail rather than mechanism.

diagnosis_patterns.observed_pattern: A condition helps explain hazardous accumulation or exposure formation.
diagnosis_patterns.diagnosis_interpretation: Reviewer reframed this condition as causally contributory, so it should not be diagnosed as isolated descriptive redundancy.
diagnosis_patterns.supporting_rule: A condition is not redundant when it contributes a supported local causal role in the pathway.
diagnosis_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: When a condition helps explain how the hazard environment forms, diagnose it as mechanism, not description.

diagnosis_patterns.observed_pattern: An attachment edge is challenged only because its connected condition was labeled redundant across types.
diagnosis_patterns.diagnosis_interpretation: The review implies the diagnosis was overcalling redundancy. If the node is not convincingly redundant, its grounding edge should not be treated as a problem.
diagnosis_patterns.supporting_rule: Only nodes truly diagnosed as descriptive-only redundancy justify follow-on cleanup of their incident edges.
diagnosis_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Do not diagnose support edges as deletable unless the connected node is first validly diagnosed as redundant.

diagnosis_patterns.observed_pattern: An edge only serves a condition already diagnosed as removable description.
diagnosis_patterns.diagnosis_interpretation: Once the condition is framed as non-causal background, its support edge is likewise nonessential to the diagnosis.
diagnosis_patterns.supporting_rule: When a descriptive-only node is removed, its incident support edge should also be removed.
diagnosis_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: After diagnosing a node as removable background detail, diagnose its attachment edge as removable too.

diagnosis_patterns.observed_pattern: Edge removal depends on a node deletion that was not sustained.
diagnosis_patterns.diagnosis_interpretation: The diagnosis preserved the condition as relevant, so the attachment edge should remain unless independently unsupported.
diagnosis_patterns.supporting_rule: Retained causally relevant conditions should keep their grounding links.
diagnosis_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Do not diagnose an attachment edge as redundant when the connected condition remains part of the mechanism.

coverage_notes: Acceptance of node_deletion_1 structurally covered edge_deletion_1, since removing C2 required removing its incident En1 -> C2 edge.

Rejection of node_deletion_2 also explains rejection of edge_deletion_2; the updated graph further reinforced C4 retention by adding a downstream causal link from High confinement to nitrogen accumulation.
